top_news.title: I accidentally turned LLM memory into program analysis
top_news.dek: A new approach applies LLM memory mechanisms to automate program analysis and vulnerability research.
top_news.brief: The author explores how to maintain state during long-running LLM agent sessions. By treating model memory as a structured component of program analysis, the system prevents agents from repeating errors or losing track of previously invalidated assumptions during codebase investigations.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual flow of LLM memory states applied to code analysis

top_news.title: FreeToken Unlocks Frontier MoE Inference on Consumer Hardware via Dynamic Co-Execution
top_news.dek: FreeToken is an open-source inference engine designed to optimize Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model performance on consumer-grade hardware.
top_news.brief: Developed by researchers at UC Berkeley and MIT, FreeToken utilizes dynamic scheduling and weight management to improve decoding speeds. The engine aims to lower the barrier for running complex reasoning systems locally on edge devices.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing dynamic scheduling of MoE model weights on consumer hardware

top_news.title: [AINews] OpenAI shuts off Cursor
top_news.dek: OpenAI's decision to cut off Cursor follows the recent acquisition of the AI code editor by SpaceX.
top_news.brief: This move mirrors previous industry shifts where model providers restrict access to tools acquired by competing entities. The termination highlights the growing tension between major AI labs and the integration of their models into third-party developer environments.
top_news.image_alt: OpenAI and SpaceX logos representing the corporate conflict

top_news.title: AI Search - AI Search now supports GLM-5.3 Flash

top_news.brief: Cloudflare has integrated GLM-5.3 Flash into its AI Search service. The model features a 1,048,576-token context window, allowing for extensive document processing and retrieval tasks within the Workers AI ecosystem.

primary.title: Google's WikiSkill gives AI agents a persistent memory of past mistakes to sharpen future performance
primary.summary: Google Research has introduced WikiSkill, a framework that gives AI agents a persistent knowledge base. Instead of discarding what they learned after each run, agents document both failures and successes in a wiki-like structure and use that knowledge to get better over time. Larger models benefit more, but smaller models with WikiSkill can match the performance of larger ones without it. The article Google's WikiSkill gives AI agents a persistent memory of past mistakes to sharpen future performance appeared first on The Decoder.

Legally, LAION can likely point to a 2024 Hamburg court ruling that allows collecting copyrighted content for non-commercial research. primary.title: AI benchmarks have a trust problem and Google wants to fix it
primary.summary: Google Deepmind is testing a double-blind evaluation of a frontier AI model for the first time. Cryptographic protection through Confidential Space is meant to keep Google from seeing the test questions and keep evaluators from seeing the model weights. The pilot project with the Singapore AI Safety Institute uses a Gemini Flash Lite and could set a new standard for tamper-proof AI benchmarks. primary.title: U.S. court rules Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic was unlawful
primary.summary: A federal court in San Francisco has ruled that the Pentagon unlawfully classified Anthropic as a supply chain risk. The Department of Defense blacklisted the company in retaliation for its public criticism of government AI policy. The designation formally remains in place because a parallel case in Washington is still pending. The ruling still sends an important signal ahead of Anthropic's planned IPO this fall.
